title: The rendered table shell uses the ARIA APG pattern that matches the surface's interactivity
iWant: the shell to render as an ARIA APG table for read-only rows and as an ARIA APG grid once cells contain interactive controls
soThat: the assistive-tech pattern matches the interactivity of the surface (ADR-1801)

acceptanceCriteria.description: Given a datatable shell that renders interactive per-row controls (sort buttons, selection checkboxes, inline actions), the rendered element is a `<table role="grid">` with `<th>` cells scoped to `col`; a read-only variant that renders no per-row interactive controls stays on the plain `<table>` pattern. The check reads the accessibility tree at the shell route and asserts the presence of the grid role when the shell ships interactive controls.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a datatable route that ships interactive per-row controls
acceptanceCriteria.then: the rendered table has `role="grid"` and header cells scoped to `col`

acceptanceCriteria.description: Given a rendered datatable, every per-row inline action (edit, delete, resend) has an accessible name that includes the acted-on row's identifier or a semantically equivalent noun (not `Edit` alone); the accessible name is readable by assistive tech per WCAG 4.1.2.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a rendered datatable with per-row inline actions
acceptanceCriteria.when: assistive tech reads the action controls
acceptanceCriteria.then: each action's accessible name identifies the acted-on row

acceptanceCriteria.description: Given a rendered datatable, the header row exposes each column's role (`<th scope="col">` or `role="columnheader"`) and every data cell resolves to a column header for row-and-column readouts on assistive tech (WCAG 1.3.1).
acceptanceCriteria.when: assistive tech traverses a data cell
acceptanceCriteria.then: the announced context includes the column header the cell resolves to
